chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The waiting period (iddah) of the woman whose husband dies is the later of the two terms, because upon her is that she should mourn for four months and ten (days), and it is not upon her with the divorce that she should mourn.

key_terms.آخِرُ الْأَجَلَيْنِ: The later of the two terms
key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: The woman whose husband has died

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a pregnant widow according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of iddah for a pregnant widow by establishing the principle of 'later of the two terms' (آخِرُ الْأَجَلَيْنِ), ensuring the period covers both the duration of pregnancy and the standard four months and ten days. It highlights the juristic distinction between death and divorce, noting that while iddah is obligatory in both, the specific mourning duration differs, reflecting the comprehensive legal methodology of the Imams. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the exact end of the waiting period when pregnancy is involved.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The waiting period of the woman widowed from her husband is the later of the two terms, because upon her is that she would mourn for four months and ten (days), and it is not upon her with the divorce that she should mourn’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The waiting period of a widow ends with the end of one of the two which ends last because she must sit in mourning for four months and ten days, while in divorce there is no mourning.’”
